Fifteen years after the 2011 uprising that toppled Muammar Gaddafi, Libya remains fragmented. Rival eastern and western power centres prevent total collapse but block meaningful national reconciliation, institutional unification and democratic transition. Instability fuels arms trafficking, organised crime, irregular migration, terrorism and foreign fighter movements across the Sahel and beyond. stories.summary: Botswana: BOB Holds Inflation Outlook Above Target Range 31 August 2026 Botswana Daily News (Gaborone) By Thato Mosinyi Gaborone — Bank of Botswana says headline inflation has eased to 9.4 per cent in July 2026, down from 10.7 per cent in June, though it remains above the central bank's medium-term objective range of three to six percent. Delivering the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) statement recently, the bank's governor, Mr Lesego Moseki attributed the decline primarily to the downward adjustment of domestic fuel prices on July 7, which shaved 2.3 percentage points off headline inflation. Mr Moseki said despite the July drop, the MPC expected inflation to stay above the target range until the first quarter of 2027 due to persistent supply-side pressures, including high fuel costs and elevated electricity tariffs. He added that projections indicated that inflation would average 7.9 per cent in 2026 before easing into the target range at an average of 4.9 per cent in 2027. He also noted that risks to the inflation outlook remained tilted to the upside, mainly reflecting potential second-round effects stemming from higher domestic fuel prices and electricity tariffs.

The probe lands at a sensitive moment for Somalia's armed forces, which are locked in an intensifying offensive against Al-Shabaab across multiple regions. Any confirmed breach of prisoner-of-war protections could complicate ties with international partners who fund and train SNAF units, and would test the military's willingness to discipline its own ranks publicly. At least 10 prisoners have died in recent weeks, as temperatures across Tunisia approached 50 degrees Celsius (122 degrees Fahrenheit) in some cities, including five prisoners who died in a single day in prisons in the greater Tunis area. Rights groups and prisoners' families have reported severe overcrowding, water and electricity cuts, inadequate ventilation, and limited access to medical care. "The deaths of 10 prisoners amid Tunisia's severe heatwave make the continued imprisonment of journalists Zied el-Heni, Mourad Zghidi, and Borhen Bsaies even more alarming," said CPJ Regional Director Sara Qudah. "These journalists should never have been imprisoned for their journalism and practicing their right in free speech. Tunisian authorities must not compound that injustice by leaving them exposed to dangerous prison conditions. They must release the three journalists immediately." In Europe, Russia's-Ukraine war remained intense despite renewed diplomatic contacts involving Washington and Moscow. Africa faced several overlapping challenges, including a worsening Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo, continuing conflict and infrastructure destruction in Sudan, and the deepening security and humanitarian crisis in Haiti.

stories.title: Somali piracy surges as the impact of the US-Iran war ripples outwards
stories.summary: Image source, AFP via Getty Images Image caption, Pirates manage to board ships operating a long way from the coast and then guide them closer to the shore By Barbara Plett Usher Africa correspondent Published 29 August 2026 Updated 31 August 2026 A surge in piracy near Somalia has increased threats to shipping already under pressure from maritime blockades and conflict due to the US war with Iran. Two cargo vessels were seized in the Gulf of Aden within four days last week, rising to at least 13 the number of ships attacked since the start of the year and triggering unprecedented drone strikes against the pirates. It is the biggest escalation in hijackings in more than a decade, renewing concern about security in this region vital to international trade. Il était issu d’une grande famille nomade dont tous les membres ne partageaient pas, loin de là, ses positions sur la question du Sahara.

stories.title: Raffinerie Dangote : les Bourses africaines sont-elles prêtes à absorber une introduction à cinq milliards de dollars ?
stories.summary: Les investisseurs nigérians se délestent d’actifs pour se positionner sur l’introduction en Bourse de la raffinerie Dangote. Les acteurs financiers francophones se montrent quant à eux plus réservés.

stories.title: DRC launches Ebola vaccination campaign as outbreak continues to spread
stories.summary: The Democratic Republic of Congo has begun vaccinating people against Ebola in Kisangani, as the country battles an outbreak that has been affecting the country since mid-May.

stories.title: Zimbabwe: At least 27 people dead after minibus and truck collide head on
stories.summary: A minibus carrying churchgoers collided head-on with a truck in central Zimbabwe, killing at least 27 people, police said Saturday, in the latest deadly road crash to hit the country.

stories.title: People fleeing Sudan civil war face ‘dire and deteriorating’ conditions in refuge city
stories.summary: Save the Children, citing government figures, says more than 200,000 people fled to El Obeid in the first half of the year. Photograph: AFP/Getty Images View image in fullscreen Save the Children, citing government figures, says more than 200,000 people fled to El Obeid in the first half of the year. Photograph: AFP/Getty Images People fleeing Sudan civil war face ‘dire and deteriorating’ conditions in refuge city More traumatised civilians are arriving every day at ‘shockingly overcrowded’ El Obeid and camps on its outskirts Humanitarian conditions in the Sudanese city of El Obeid and two camps on its outskirts are dire and deteriorating, according to people on the ground, as civilians displaced by fighting between the Sudanese Armed Forces and Rapid Support Forces (RSF) militia continue to pour in from the surrounding countryside. The UN says more than 15,000 families have arrived since mid-July, joining more than 200,000 people who arrived in the first half of the year, according to government figures cited by Save the Children. “The situation is very harsh and is deteriorating as El Obeid is receiving IDPs [internally displaced people] on a daily basis … The city is shockingly overcrowded,” said Maryam, a humanitarian volunteer whose name has been changed for her safety. The new arrivals came on foot, carrying almost nothing, she said. “They also suffer from a shortage of food and they definitely arrive traumatised.” The city, the capital of North Kordofan province, was home to around half a million people before the war broke out more than three years ago.

stories.title: En Guinée-Bissau, un référendum constitutionnel et l’ombre du président déchu
stories.summary: A trois mois de l’élection présidentielle, le général Horta N’Tam, arrivé à la tête du pays par un putsch, en novembre 2025, entend instaurer un régime présidentiel à la place du régime parlementaire en vigueur. L’opposition a appelé au boycott du scrutin.

stories.title: La Somalie et la Turquie libèrent un cargo détourné au terme d’une opération meurtrière ; le Puntland dénonce le paiement d’une rançon
stories.summary: Cette opération a été menée dans un contexte de recrudescence des actes de piraterie au large de la Somalie, où au moins 15 attaques ont été recensées depuis le début de l’année, d’après une analyse de données de l’Organisation maritime internationale.

stories.title: Soldiers in Niger Attack Presidential Palace and Airport, Shaking Junta
stories.summary: Renegade Nigerien soldiers attacked sites around the capital, the defense ministry said, including a key air base that hosts Russian mercenaries.

stories.title: En RDC, quand les camps Kabila et Bemba s’affrontaient à Kinshasa en août 2006
stories.summary: Le 30 juillet 2006, la RDC organise ses premières présidentielles libres depuis l’indépendance. Après l’annonce des résultats du premier tour, des affrontements éclatent entre partisans de Joseph Kabila et de Jean-Pierre Bemba. Fidèle Babala, alors directeur de campagne de ce dernier, livre son récit des événements.

stories.title: Algérie : le président Tebboune veut appliquer la peine de mort contre les pyromanes
stories.summary: Publicité Algérie : le président Tebboune veut appliquer la peine de mort contre les pyromanes Afrique Le président algérien Abdelmadjid Tebboune a annoncé dimanche vouloir rétablir l'application de la peine de mort contre les pyromanes, après les incendies meurtriers qui ont ravagé l'est et le nord du pays. L'Algérie observe un moratoire sur la peine de mort depuis 1993. Publié le : 31/08/2026 - 09:00 2 min Temps de lecture Partager Par : FRANCE 24 Le président algérien Abdelmadjid Tebboune lors d'une conférence de presse à Berlin en Allemagne, le 16 juillet 2026. © John Macdougall, AFP Le président algérien Abdelmadjid Tebboune – dont le pays observe un moratoire sur la peine de mort depuis 1993 – a annoncé dimanche 30 août vouloir rétablir son application contre les pyromanes, après les incendies meurtriers qui ont ravagé l'est et le nord de l' Algérie cet été. S'adressant au ministre de la Justice lors d'une réunion consacrée aux feux en présence de hauts responsables civils et militaires, le chef de l'État algérien a ordonné "une modification du Code pénal" avant le 15 septembre. Abdelmadjid Tebboune a demandé à ce que le projet passe par le gouvernement, puis que le Parlement l'étudie "rapidement". "On réinstaure la condamnation à mort pour les pyromanes", a-t-il déclaré. "Il y aura exécution" une fois les voies de recours épuisées pour les condamnés, a-t-il insisté dans des images retransmises à la télévision.

stories.title: Guinée : Algassimou Diallo, la chute d’un magistrat jadis porté aux nues
stories.summary: Un enregistrement à l’authenticité controversée a précipité la chute de celui qui, pendant le procès du massacre du 28-Septembre, a porté l’accusation. stories.title: Le championnat libyen de football retrouve son attractivité avec des transferts record, malgré une situation politique chaotique
stories.summary: Disposant de moyens financiers considérables, plusieurs clubs libyens attirent désormais des internationaux africains à coups de transferts et de salaires record. Une ambition qui contraste avec la fragilité politique et sécuritaire persistante d’un pays coupé en deux.

stories.summary: Contrôles, encadrement voire suspension des permis… Depuis le drame de Zamboï, les autorités de Bangui s’attèlent à remettre de l’ordre dans la filière aurifère. Une tâche difficile quand on connaît les méfaits de l’économie informelle.

stories.title: Turkey and Israel Vie for Middle East Influence as Tensions Spike
stories.summary: Israel’s strike on a Syrian base to pre-empt the feared deployment of Turkish forces was part of a growing competition in the Middle East and beyond.

stories.title: Oligui Nguema traque les avoirs des Bongo, Tshisekedi impose son tempo, le RNI et le PAM se déchirent… Les 5 infos qu’il ne fallait pas manquer

stories.title: Entre le Maroc et l’Espagne, la crise de Ceuta ressuscite le contentieux frontalier
stories.summary: Près d’un mois après les traversées illégales massives vers l’enclave espagnole, une violente bataille informationnelle oppose les médias des deux pays, replongeant Rabat et Madrid dans une crise qui ne dit pas son nom.

stories.title: Les plages de Dakar, polluées et jonchées de plastique, victimes de la croissance de la ville
stories.summary: Alors que la période des chaleurs et des pluies court jusqu’à octobre, les plages de la capitale sénégalaise voient affluer familles et surfeurs mais aussi les déchets et les eaux usées charriés par une métropole en pleine croissance.

stories.title: Le canal de Suez, un laissez-passer pour les espèces invasives en Méditerranée
stories.summary: « Suez, canal historique » (6/6). La création de l’axe maritime au XIXᵉ siècle a favorisé la migration d’espèces dites « lessepsiennes », d’après le nom du « père » du canal, depuis la mer Rouge jusqu’à la Grande Bleue. Elles prolifèrent, favorisées par la surpêche, la pollution, la construction côtière et l’accélération du réchauffement climatique.

stories.title: Marc Alexandre Oho Bambe : un nouveau recueil de poésie et un nouvel album
stories.summary: Poète, romancier, slameur et désormais plus que jamais musicien : Marc Alexandre Oho Bambe, alias Capitaine Alexandre, est l’invité du Journal de l’Afrique. À 50 ans, l’artiste né à Douala ouvre un nouveau chapitre de sa création. Côté littérature, il publie chez Mémoire d’encrier Poèmes de plein jour et mots mantras pour traverser la nuit, des textes pour affronter les vertiges de notre époque sans renoncer à la lumière. Côté musique, il change de tempo avec Salsa Makossa, l’un des premiers titres de son album anniversaire. Une rencontre entre les mots, les rythmes, le Cameroun et cette question qui traverse son œuvre : comment résister au fracas du monde sans renoncer à la joie ?

stories.title: En Guinée, les soupçons d’exécutions extrajudiciaires se renforcent après la découverte de nouveaux corps
stories.summary: Alors que les cas de disparitions forcées se multiplient dans le pays depuis le putsch du général Mamadi Doumbouya, le 5 septembre 2021, six corps ont été découverts, lundi 24 août, dans une fosse commune à Sabakhouré.

Authorities in the capital released pictures of the suspects captured by security cameras during the heist at the Museum of Applied Arts (MAK), amid a rash of spectacular smash-and-grab thefts from European cultural institutions. stories.title: Africa's aging autocrats fight to stay in power
stories.summary: https://p.dw.com/p/5JK6k Backed by a loyal inner circle, Paul Biya (center) was sworn in for an eighth term as president of Cameroon in November 2025 Image: Angel Ngwe/AP Photo/picture alliance Advertisement Power can be seductive, and many who possess it want to hold on for as long as possible. The leaders of China and Russia , for example, cleared the way for additional terms years ago, and in the United States, the president occasionally speaks of another run for office, even though the US Constitution does not allow it. From the perspective of Paul Biya, however, Chinese President Xi Jinping , Russian President Vladimir Putin and US President Donald Trump are still relatively new to office. Cameroon's president has been head of state since 1982. In 2025, Biya began his eighth term — which is officially due to end on November 6, 2032, just a few months before his 100th birthday.

stories.title: World's youngest reigning traditional monarch dies aged 34
stories.summary: Image source, AFP via Getty Images Image caption, King Oyo ascended to the throne at the age of three but was crowned on reaching adulthood at 18 in 2010 By Swaibu Ibrahim BBC Africa ,Â Reporting from Kampala Published 28 August 2026 A traditional Ugandan ruler named as the world's youngest monarch has died aged 34, his prime minister has announced. Oyo Nyimba Kabamba Iguru Rukidi IV became king of Tooro in western Uganda at just three years old in 1995 after the death of his father. The Tooro kingdom did not disclose the cause of King Oyo's death, but a Ugandan government minister was quoted in local media saying that he had been critically ill and was seeking treatment in the US. Though Uganda is governed by an elected president and parliament, it has several traditional kingdoms which continue to have significant cultural influence despite not having political power. Oyo, who Guinness World Records listed as the world's youngest reigning monarch , external , ruled over more than two million people.

stories.summary: https://p.dw.com/p/5JOcT The far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) is leading strongly in the polls and hopes to form a state government for the first time Image: M. Gränzdörfer/Agentur Matthias Wehnert/IMAGO Advertisement The Saxony-Anhalt state election on September 6 could make history. For the first time, the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) could become the strongest party in a German state by winning the vote. The AfD is currently leading the polls at over 40% , far ahead of the center-right Christian Democrats (CDU) of Chancellor Friedrich Merz at around 24%. The AfD advocates a restrictive immigration policy centered on sharply reducing migration , increasing deportations and promoting what it calls "remigration," while also emphasizing national sovereignty, cultural identity and traditional family values.

stories.title: 'If you started running, they shot you' - inside Nigeria's growing kidnapping crisis
stories.summary: Image caption, Fatima says her husband and six of his siblings were killed when bandits attacked By Yemisi Adegoke BBC Africa ,Â Reporting from Zamfara and Oyo states Published 27 August 2026 "If you ran into a room, they set the room on fire," says Fatima, describing a recent attack on her village in Zamfara, north-western Nigeria. "If you came out and started running, they shot you." The gunmen, who struck at 02:00, split into groups to surround residents: one at the village entrance, one in the centre and one at the back. "They opened fire without a care in the world, shooting indiscriminately," the 55-year-old quietly tells the BBC World Service. It was one of many attacks that have caused havoc in the mainly Muslim community where residents live in fear of being kidnapped for ransom. Fatima explains how the raids unfold: "You could have 100 motorcycles, and each one could be carrying three people." About 70 people, including children, were killed from the village of Bia Buki in June, according to Fatima. She describes how the attackers also targeted villagers as they fled and children were injured falling into ditches. Among the dead were her husband and six of his seven siblings.

stories.summary: Image source, EPA By James Gallagher ,Â Health and science correspondent Â and Â Emery Makumeno ,Â BBC Africa ,Â Reporting from Kinshasa Published 18 May 2026 Updated 25 August 2026 The current Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo is now the deadliest of the 17 the country has faced as it continues to spread. United Nations experts have described it as the fastest growing outbreak on record in terms of new infections. Getting the spread of the deadly virus under control is challenging because it involves a rare species of Ebola for which there is no vaccine - though some are being tested - and the epicentre is in an area affected by conflict. What is Ebola and what are the symptoms? Ebola is a rare but deadly disease caused by a virus.
